status: Development mechanism study on two familiar ranger worlds; new keyed schedules are not fresh-world validation.
objective: Measure the value of repeated enemy NPC review beyond fixed plan selection, and continued access to planner history and notes after shared initialization.
schedule: New v2 streams include case seed/index, calibration/evaluation partition and calibration repetition. Warm-up and stable are 90% A; recurring is 90% A, then 90% B at a keyed round in 6..8, then 90% A at a keyed round in 17..19. Mixture draws are sampled, never rerolled. All evaluation arms and model repetitions share a realized case/history schedule. Timing, labels, seeds and future observations are hidden from planners.
calibration: Before any evaluation, run all seven complete fixed plans through both histories in each of two separately keyed calibration repetitions per case. Each repetition shares ten warm-ups and an identical restored checkpoint across plans/histories. Select one plan per case by mean damage, weighting both histories and repetitions equally, ties in catalog order. Use that same plan in both evaluation histories. This informed static benchmark receives extra simulator experience; it is not an equal-resource or equal-information planner comparison. Preserve every calibration fight and freeze winners before evaluation.

arms.retained: Default NPC plan, ordinary Rust learning throughout.
arms.fixed: The complete calibrated plan stays fixed; ordinary Rust tactic choice and learning continue where the plan allows them.
arms.initial: Two branches hold their paired agent's first selected complete plan for all rounds. An initial failure holds baseline. No further model calls.
arms.full: Two agent repetitions review all completed warm-up and own branch fights, plus previous bounded note, before each round.
arms.recent: Two paired agent repetitions share the full arm's initial request, decision and first fight. From round two, each fresh request sees only its own latest completed fight, current plan and public round clock; previous notes, reasons, predictions and earlier observations are excluded. Output notes are recorded but never fed back.

initialization: Run one shared ten-fight evaluation warm-up per case. For each case/history/model repetition, make one initial request using these ten rounds and baseline plan with empty note. Apply its decision to full, recent and initial arms from identical checkpoint/RNG. Charge the shared request once. All first fights must match exactly, including resulting policy state.
observationBoundary: Both agent arms omit policy cells, scores, counts and probabilities, including the common initial request. This differs from v1 and prevents policy summaries becoming a second planner-history channel. Full versus recent changes access to chronological observations and explicit notes together. Both receive the same menu/rules and true round number. No case IDs, seeds, hidden labels, schedule, coordinates, counterfactuals, other branches or previous reasoning/predictions. Rust itself retains learned state; currentPlanId and the latest action still carry consequences of earlier choices. This is not a globally memory-free comparison.
controls: Reuse v1's exact seven ranger plans and physics. No new actions, memory edits, stat buffs, generated code or simulated probes. Every fixed and agent round uses normal Rust choose, legal masks, feedback and commit. A held auto-choice plan may still choose different aim/lead tactics. Opponent inputs may respond to different NPC behavior.

agent.sampling: Provider defaults; fresh isolated CLI process for each unique request. No exposed temperature or seed control.

failurePolicy: Invalid or failed calls retain previous validated plan and permitted note; shared initialization failure retains baseline in all three branches. No repair calls. Admission and cost reservations are atomic, with a persisted latched stop after three consecutive completed provider failures. Pending unknown-outcome calls on resume become recorded fallbacks, never resent. Dispatch in round waves across every case/history/repetition, at most four calls concurrently, rotating order by round. Preserve partial data on budget exhaustion or errors and mark incomplete; do not reduce repetitions/horizon after seeing results. Provider costs are CLI-reported and per-request caps may be exceeded in flight.

budget.formula: Calibration: 2 cases * 2 repetitions * (10 warmups + 2 histories * 7 plans * 24 rounds). Evaluation: 2 cases * (10 warmups + 2 histories * (retained + calibrated fixed + 2 initial + 2 full + 2 recent) * 24 rounds). Calls: 2 cases * 2 histories * 2 repetitions * (1 shared initial + 2 * 23 subsequent reviews).

analysis: Three primary descriptive contrasts: full minus calibrated-fixed; full minus paired held-initial; full minus paired recent-only. Include all post-warmup fights, exploration and failures. Average model repetitions within each case/history, then cases equally. Report raw damage and paired trajectories, per-repetition differences, defeats, survival, plan changes, cost and latency. Clock windows 1..6,7..18,19..24 are secondary descriptive summaries, not oracle recovery metrics. No p-values, confidence intervals, best-run exclusion or regret based on old two-tactic tables.
claimLimits: Two familiar worlds support development interpretation only. Full versus held-initial measures repeated review beyond that realized first selection; full versus calibrated-fixed compares against a deliberately informed static benchmark with extra calibration experience. Full versus recent estimates continued access to the joint history/note package after common initialization, not notes alone or all memory. Rust learning and action-mediated state remain. Model repetitions are nested trajectories, not independent worlds. New schedules do not make unseen-world validation. Exact replay uses recorded model outputs, not identical regeneration.
publication: Freeze protocol, source fingerprints and calibration selection before evaluation model calls. Publish filtered observations, decisions, failures, all calibration/evaluation outcomes and offline verification. Exclude raw provider sessions, credentials and personal paths. Preserve v1 evidence and the playable game controller.
